newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 15.

text.p: There are 77 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

The HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES said clarification of the right of abode was good news for Hong Kong people. But the Sino-British confrontation in the last few months before the handover could not help but add to local anxieties regarding a smooth transition, the paper said.

The Beijing-backed WEN WEI PO said Britain had been trapped on the right of abode issue and many other transitional matters because it refused to recognise the provisional legislature. Asking for the publication of a white paper on the right of abode before allowing the provisional legislature to pass the laws was an indirect way of recognising the council, it said.

The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said the decision on right of abode was generous, both in the time allowed and in recognising dual nationality. But it was extremely frustrating that Britain and China agreed on the details only to disagree on implementation. The interests of Hong Kong people appear to have been given the usual low priority, it said.
